assessment.headline: DAY 31. Pentagon plans ground ops. Both chokepoints at risk. But 6 Indian carriers crossed. The paradox deepens.
assessment.body:
The war is simultaneously escalating (Pentagon planning ground raids on Kharg Island, Houthis threatening Bab al-Mandeb, nuclear scientists killed, NPT exit pushed) AND showing diplomatic cracks (4-way Islamabad talks, Trump claiming Iran agreed to 'most' demands, 20 Pakistani ships transiting).

For India specifically — VERIFIED FACTS:
• 28 Indian ships were near Hormuz at war's peak → 20 remain with 540 seafarers
• 6 carriers have safely crossed: Shivalik, Nanda Devi (Mar 14), Pine Gas, Jag Vasant (Mar 25), + 2 SCI carriers (Mar 28)
• Op Urja Suraksha: 5+ Navy warships escorting through Gulf of Oman
• Iran FM on Mar 26 explicitly listed India among nations allowed passage
• BUT: 91% of LPG still Gulf-dependent. Only a fraction of monthly need covered

The DUAL CHOKEPOINT THREAT is the gravest development for India. If Houthis block Bab al-Mandeb (Red Sea), ships can't even reroute around Hormuz via the Cape of Good Hope and Suez. India's ENTIRE maritime energy supply chain would be severed.

Economic damage is now structural: FII outflow ₹1,13,810 Cr (largest ever monthly). Rupee 94.79 ATL. RBI burned $15B. Excise cut ₹10/L ('huge revenue hit'). Indian basket $125/bbl. Market down 12% YTD. PhonePe halted IPO.

CSMonitor: 'India is the biggest loser in a war it isn't even fighting.' EPW: 'strategic autonomy squandered.' Pakistan mediates. India gets selective passage but is absent from diplomacy.

April 6 = 7 days. Ground ops are being planned. If Kharg is seized, Iran could retaliate against Indian assets in the Gulf. If talks succeed, massive relief. India is walking a tightrope between being a key buyer that Iran needs — and a nation with 10 million citizens in a war zone.
